meta.name: LinkPass Enterprise On-Premises Deployment Specification
meta.author: SyncGlide Enterprise
meta.description: Standard architectural requirements, packaging bundles, security constraints, and operational workflows for deploying LinkPass in isolated on-premises enterprise environments.

core_principles: Zero-Knowledge First: server never handles unencrypted client secrets or private key material
Zero Source Code Shipped: only compiled binaries, container images, or minified static assets are distributed — no raw source
Air-Gapped Autonomy: zero required internet dependencies; licensing verified offline via asymmetric RS256 RSA keys
Deployment Flexibility: supports both Docker Compose containerized and host-native Linux deployments
Auditability: security-relevant actions are logged with an immutable 90-day retention period

deployment_strategy.rationale: Docker Compose provides an isolated, single-command deployment path across Ubuntu and RHEL without dependency conflicts, while host-native systemd support fits strict corporate environments where Docker is restricted.

contents: server/ (FastAPI application engine, router modules, middleware)
server/license_pub.pem (Production RSA Public Key for offline RS256 JWT validation)
server/certs/ (SSL/TLS certificate store for HTTPS execution)
docker-compose.yml (Container orchestration manifest with SQLite and PostgreSQL HA options)
bundles.installation_method: unzip LinkPass-Linux-Server.zip -d LinkPass && cd LinkPass && cp /path/to/license.jwt server/ && sudo docker compose up --build -d

contents: cacert.pem (Custom corporate SSL/TLS root certificate trust bundle)
bundles.installation_method: uncompress LinkPass-Client.zip -> update config.json with Linux server IP -> launch LinkPass.exe

contents: KeyGen/linkpass_private_key.pem (RSA 2048-bit Private Signing Key — KEEP STRICTLY CONFIDENTIAL)
bundles.installation_method: Run python main.py on secure air-gapped machine to generate client `.lic` files

build_pipeline.build_environment: Windows / Linux build runner with PyInstaller & Docker Engine 24+

packaging: zip -r LinkPass-Linux-Server.zip server/ docker-compose.yml docs/ README.md

default_tier.use_case: Small to Medium Enterprise deployments (Up to 500 active users)

scaled_tier.network_restriction: localhost or internal-subnet only, TLS required

networking_and_firewall.airgap_compliance: fully offline. Zero outbound internet calls required for core function.

licensing_verification.cryptography: RSA-2048 / RS256 algorithm via PyJWT signature verification
licensing_verification.failure_behavior: Returns HTTP 403 Forbidden with license error payload

encryption_model.key_management: Private key (linkpass_private_key.pem) resides exclusively on SecOps air-gapped machine; server only holds public key (license_pub.pem)

authentication.first_boot_bootstrap: Initial superadmin account ('admin') TOTP secret is printed to console log on first container execution

host_hardening.process_isolation: Backend process runs inside isolated container environment as non-privileged app instance
host_hardening.db_network_isolation: Internal Docker bridge network or localhost only; non-routable externally

governance_and_audit.approval_model: multi-admin quorum (threshold signature approval, e.g., 2 of 3 admins)

initial_deployment: 1. Transfer LinkPass-Linux-Server.zip to target host via SCP/SFTP
2. Extract bundle: unzip LinkPass-Linux-Server.zip -d LinkPass && cd LinkPass
3. Copy client license file into LinkPass/server/license.jwt
4. Start service: sudo docker compose up --build -d
5. Retrieve initial admin TOTP seed from logs: sudo docker compose logs server
6. Open required port 443 on host firewall (sudo ufw allow 443/tcp or firewall-cmd)
7. Distribute client bundle (LinkPass-Client.zip) and updated config.json to workstations
update_or_renewal: 1. Generate new .lic file via KeyGen tool on air-gapped SecOps workstation
2. Replace LinkPass/server/license.jwt on Linux server host
3. Restart backend service: sudo docker compose restart server
backup_and_recovery: Database snapshot: Backup linkpass.db file or run pg_dump for PostgreSQL
Verification & restore: Use decrypt_backup.py CLI tool to extract and verify database backup integrity

compliance_checklist: No raw source code present on deployed hosts
No outbound internet calls required for core function
All secrets/keys excluded from version control and bundles
TLS enabled on all exposed ports
Audit logging enabled and retention period documented
